name: Castries Centre
tagline: The working capital around its harbour
description: Saint Lucia's capital, built around a deep harbour that takes cruise ships, with the Castries Central Market, Derek Walcott Square and the cathedral. It is busy and functional by day and empties once the ships and the offices close.
bestFor: Anyone needing banks, the market and the island bus routes
pros: The market is the best on the island
Derek Walcott Square and the cathedral
cons: Hot, busy and short on shade
Almost no accommodation aimed at long stays

name: Rodney Bay
tagline: Where the long-stay visitors actually live
description: A developed bay in the north with a marina, a shopping mall, the island's concentration of restaurants and bars, and Reduit Beach along its western side. It is where most remote workers, yachties and long-stay visitors base themselves rather than in Castries.
bestFor: Remote workers wanting services, restaurants and a beach together
pros: The island's best concentration of restaurants and services
Best internet and apartment stock on the island
cons: The most expensive area in Saint Lucia
Built for visitors rather than locals

name: Gros Islet
tagline: The village behind the bay, and the Friday street party
description: The fishing village immediately north of Rodney Bay, considerably cheaper and more local, and the site of the Friday night street party that is Saint Lucia's longest-running institution. Pigeon Island is at the end of the causeway beyond it.
bestFor: Budget stays wanting Rodney Bay's amenities at village prices
pros: Much cheaper than Rodney Bay next door

name: Soufriere
tagline: Under the Pitons, and worth the drive
description: The town on the southwest coast beneath the Pitons, with the drive-in volcano and sulphur springs, botanical gardens and waterfalls around it, and the best diving on the island at Anse Chastanet. It is ninety minutes from Castries on a spectacular road.
bestFor: Anyone whose reason for coming is the Pitons and the diving
pros: The Pitons and the sulphur springs at the door
cons: Ninety minutes from Castries on hairpins

name: Marigot Bay
tagline: The hurricane hole that looks like a film set
description: A narrow inlet halfway down the west coast, almost enclosed by a palm-covered spit, used as a hurricane refuge by sailors for centuries and as a location for the 1967 Doctor Dolittle film. It holds a marina, a handful of resorts and very little else.
bestFor: Sailors and anyone wanting a quiet, beautiful anchorage
pros: One of the most sheltered bays in the Caribbean
Marina, restaurants and a ferry across the inlet
cons: The beach is modest by island standards
